structure: Part 2 of repo:stub, MDM countries and ports stubs. Read in full: stubs/mdm/countries (CountriesController, 34 lines, and the MdmCountry, MdmBlock, MdmSubDivision and MdmCodedValue records), stubs/mdm/poe (PortsOfEntryController, 32 lines, and the MdmPortsResponse and MdmPortOfEntry records), utils/FileUtils (30 lines) and FileUtilsTest (77 lines, 5 tests), the two fixtures responses/countriesResponse.json (772 lines, 31 country records, every field read) and responses/portsOfEntryResponse.json (82 lines, 78 ports), the mdm block of application.yml (lines 139 to 152) and the MDM rows of README.md's latency and fault tables (lines 11 to 16 and 40 to 43). Layout: two GET endpoints, each answers with a classpath JSON fixture loaded per request through FileUtils, with a fixed trace header; neither filters on its query parameters. Covered: both endpoints' paths, the required subscription-key header, the system and blocks parameters and what the stub does with them, the response header and wrapper, every record field, every country (one claim each, with codes, long name, subdivisions and block), the fixture-wide values (one block, independence, status, system), all 78 ports in fixture order with their duplicates and copy oddities, FileUtils' loading and failure behaviour, every FileUtilsTest test, the MDM latency metadata for the two paths, the README's MDM rows, and gaps against what the live-animals and germinal-products journeys need from countries and ports (block membership, non-European countries, port type and commodity designation, subdivision blocs, controller tests). Latency profiles and fault injection themselves are left to their out-of-scope tooling; the address lookup simulator is part 1.

claims.statement: The stub answers GET /mdm/geo/countries, standing in for MDM's countries reference-data call.
The countries endpoint requires an Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key request header; Spring rejects a request without it, so a call with no key is refused (a bad request) rather than answered.
claims.note: The header is required by default (@RequestHeader with no required=false). The 400 outcome is Spring's default for a missing required header, not code in the stub.

claims.statement: The countries endpoint accepts any subscription-key value: the key is read but never checked, so any non-empty value gets the full answer.
claims.note: Inferred because the method body never uses ocpApimSubscriptionKey.

claims.statement: The countries endpoint takes an optional system query parameter but ignores it: the same list comes back whatever system is asked for.
claims.note: Inferred because the method body never uses system.

claims.statement: The countries endpoint takes an optional blocks query parameter but does not filter on it: every call returns the whole fixture, whichever block is asked for or if none is.
claims.note: Inferred because blocks is never read in the method body. Outside this slice, trade-imports-reference-data's MdmService passes system GBNAG and blocks to MDM and then filters the answer by block itself (isIncludedInRequestedBlock), so on the stack the filtering a user sees is done by reference-data, not by the stub.

claims.statement: The countries endpoint answers 200 OK with a JSON array of country records read from responses/countriesResponse.json.
The countries endpoint sets the response header x-ms-middleware-request-id to the fixed value stub-trace-id.

Each country record carries name, longName, effectiveAlpha2, effectiveAlpha3, effectiveAlias, effectiveLongName, independent (a boolean), statusName, system, systemAlias, systemAlpha2, systemAlpha3, systemLongName, a list of subDivisions and a list of blocks.
A country's block membership is a record of the block name, an includeCountry boolean and a list of string tags.
A subdivision record carries a code (an object holding a single value string), a name and a list of blocs (spelt blocs, not blocks).
The countries fixture holds 31 country records, in alphabetical order of name from Austria to Switzerland, so the stub always returns these 31 countries in that order.
claims.note: Counted with jq (length 31). Records 012 to 042 name each one.

claims.note: Checked across all 31 records with jq.

claims.statement: Every country in the fixture is marked independent false, including sovereign states such as Germany and France.
claims.note: Checked across all 31 records. Real MDM data would mark these states independent, so the stub value is fixture data, not a meaningful flag.

claims.statement: Every country in the fixture has statusName officially-assigned and system iso, with systemAlias, systemAlpha2, systemAlpha3 and systemLongName all null.
claims.note: The caller (reference-data) asks for system GBNAG, but the fixture's records all say system iso.

claims.statement: In every country record effectiveAlias is the same as name, and effectiveLongName is the same as longName.

claims.statement: The fixture's countries are the 27 EU member states plus Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway and Switzerland: no country outside Europe is offered by the stub.
claims.note: Inferred by comparing the 31 names with the EU and EFTA memberships; the fixture itself does not say so. The block name GBNAG_SPS_EX suggests an SPS export-country list for GBN-AG, but the fixture never explains it.

claims.statement: Country names come in their ISO short-name form, so the Netherlands appears as "Netherlands (the)" and the Czech Republic as "Czechia".

Only three countries have subdivisions: France (6: Martinique, Guadeloupe, Saint Martin (French part), Reunion, French Guiana, Mayotte), Portugal (2: Madeira, Azores) and Spain (1: Canary Islands); the other 28 have an empty subDivisions list.
No subdivision in the fixture carries a blocs list, so the stub never says which block a subdivision belongs to; each holds only a code and a name.
claims.note: Inferred from the record defining blocs while none of the nine subdivision entries in the fixture sets it, so it deserialises as null.

claims.statement: The stub answers GET /mdm/trade/bcp/poes, standing in for MDM's border control post (ports of entry) reference-data call.
The ports endpoint requires an Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key request header but never checks its value, so any key gets the full answer and a call with no key is refused.
claims.note: That the value is unchecked is read from the method body, which never uses it.

claims.statement: The ports endpoint takes an optional system query parameter and ignores it, and reads no other parameter, so it cannot filter ports by type, commodity or anything else.
claims.quote:
@RequestParam(value = "system", required = false) String system) {

    MdmPortsResponse response = fileUtils.getObjectFromFile("responses/portsOfEntryResponse.json", MdmPortsResponse.class);
claims.note: Inferred because system is never used in the method body.

The ports endpoint sets the response header x-ms-middleware-request-id to the fixed value stub-trace-id.

claims.statement: Port ids are the strings "1" to "78", numbered in fixture order with no gaps.

The ports come roughly in alphabetical order of name but not strictly: HES Humber Bulk Terminal comes before Harwich Port, TILBURY before Teesside International Airport, and Port of Middlesbrough after Portsmouth  Port, so a page listing them in fixture order would not be fully alphabetical.

claims.statement: Every port is in Great Britain: every code starts with GB, and the list mixes airports (such as Heathrow Airport), seaports and harbours (such as Port of Dover) and docks (such as Liverpool Docks).
Pembroke Port appears twice, under codes GB PED (id 46) and GB PEM (id 47), so a port list built from the stub shows two identical names.
Port of Sheerness appears twice, under code GBSHS with no space (id 63) and GB SHS (id 64), so a port list built from the stub shows two identical names.
The port name "Portsmouth  Port" has two spaces between its words.

claims.statement: Both endpoints read their fixture from the classpath afresh on every request, so the answer is always the fixture's current content and nothing a caller does changes it.
claims.note: Inferred from the controllers calling getObjectFromFile inside the request handler with no caching.

claims.statement: If a fixture cannot be found or read, the stub logs "Failed to read from JSON file" and fails the request with the error "Failed to read from json file: <file name>" (a missing file is reported first as "File not found: <file name>").
claims.note: What HTTP status the caller then sees depends on the stub's exception handling, which is outside this slice.

claims.statement: A unit test proves the countries fixture reads as a non-empty list whose first country has a non-blank name and alpha-2 code.
A unit test proves Spain (ES) has exactly one subdivision, code ES-CN, named Canary Islands.
A unit test proves the ports fixture reads as a response whose result list is present and not empty.
A unit test proves the ports fixture holds exactly 78 ports, the first is GB DYC Aberdeen Airport, and the codes include GB EMA, GB EDI and GB DVR.
A unit test proves asking for a fixture that does not exist fails with an error containing "Failed to read from json file".
No test in this slice exercises the two endpoints over HTTP, so the required header, the ignored system and blocks parameters and the trace header are unproven here.
claims.ref: src/test/java/uk/gov/defra/trade/imports (searched with grep -rln for mdm, Countries and PortsOfEntry)
claims.note: The grep found only FileUtilsTest in scope; the other matches are the out-of-scope latency and fault tests (StubLatenciesTest, LatencyProfilesIT, FaultsIT and others), which may call these paths for their own purposes.

claims.statement: The stub's latency configuration names the MDM integration as "MDM reference data through APIM: countries and border control posts", owned by the MDM / data platform team, covering the two paths /mdm/geo/countries and /mdm/trade/bcp/poes.
claims.quote:
mdm:
      interface-name: "MDM reference data through APIM: countries and border control posts"
      owner: MDM / data platform team

claims.statement: By default the MDM paths answer with no added delay (profile zero-delay), and the interim service-level targets are p50 100 ms, p95 400 ms and p99 1,000 ms, recorded as not agreed.
claims.note: The latency profiles themselves are out of scope; this claim records only what the block says for the two MDM paths.

claims.statement: The README says the stub stands in for MDM reference data through APIM, which trade-imports-reference-data calls, on GET /mdm/geo/countries and GET /mdm/trade/bcp/poes.
claims.quote:
This stub stands in for two integrations that `trade-imports-reference-data` calls, and gives each its own latency profile:
...
| `mdm` | MDM reference data through APIM | `GET /mdm/geo/countries`, `GET /mdm/trade/bcp/poes` |

claims.statement: The README says both MDM paths can be made to fail on demand, for the resilience runs.
claims.note: The fault kinds and controls are out of scope.

claims.statement: The stub has no block other than GBNAG_SPS_EX and ignores the blocks parameter, so it cannot offer a germinal-products country list, or any list that differs between the live-animals and germinal-products journeys, on the local stack.
claims.note: Looked for any other block name in the fixture with jq and for any blocks handling in the controller; there is none. Whether germinal products need a different block is for the requirement sources to say.

claims.statement: The countries fixture offers no country outside the EU and EFTA, so a live-animals or germinal-products notification from a non-European country of origin cannot be made against the stub.
claims.note: Looked at all 31 country records. Whether the journeys need non-European origins is for the requirement sources to say.

claims.statement: Port records carry no type or transport mode (airport, seaport, road, rail), so the stub cannot narrow ports by how the consignment arrives.
claims.note: Looked at the record and all 78 fixture entries: only id, code and name. A type can only be guessed from the name.

claims.statement: Port records say nothing about which commodities a border control post is designated for (such as live animals or germinal products), so the stub cannot offer different port lists to the live-animals and germinal-products journeys.
claims.note: Looked at the record, all 78 fixture entries and the controller's parameters; there is no designation field and no filter parameter.

claims.statement: Subdivisions carry no region or block data in the fixture, so the stub cannot show whether a region such as the Canary Islands or Madeira is treated differently from its country for live animals or germinal products.
claims.note: Looked at all nine subdivision entries; none sets blocs. Whether the journeys need region-level origin is for the requirement sources to say.
